title: Feature SKU Runway: Attrition-Adjusted Pricing Catalog
content:
Executive summary:

This sheet bundles a feature-SKU oriented runway with headcount planning that explicitly models attrition, onboarding lag, and price-sensitivity across token and reserved-commit pricing. The goal is to produce a compact decision surface showing: (1) cash burn and runway by SKU under three price pivots, (2) headcount needs by role accounting for turnover and hiring lag, and (3) operational trigger rules (price or HC) to flip between reserved, burst, or routing strategies.

Key assumptions (base):
- Forecast horizon: 12 months (FY27 Q1–Q4 + Q1–Q2 2028 bridge)
- Starting runway cash: $72,000,000 (balance on 2026-11-01)
- Avg monthly token demand baseline: 18B tokens / month (weighted across hosted + dedicated customers)
- Feature- SKU mix: Search (30%), Chat (45%), Embeddings (20%), Rerank (5%)
- Avg gross margin per SKU at baseline pricing and model mix: 46%
- Average fully loaded FTE cost per finance/infra/eng role: Eng IC $24k/mo, SRE $26k/mo, Infra Eng $28k/mo, Product/PM/Design $18k/mo, Sales/CS $15k/mo, Finance/Ops $14k/mo
- Attrition: voluntary baseline 12% annualized (1.0% per month) with seasonal +0.3ppt in Q2 hiring quarters
- Hiring lag: 10 weeks on average from req to productive
- Reserved GPU commit discount: 40% vs spot for committed capacity; however commit increases fixed monthly cost and reduces marginal cost by 12% when utilization > 70%

Headcount plan (FTEs, quarter snapshots - attrition-adjusted):
- Baseline (end Q1 FY27): Eng IC 48, SRE 12, Infra Eng 10, Product 14, Sales/CS 22, Finance/Ops 8 (total 114)
- Conservative (slower hiring, +reduction): Eng IC 42, SRE 10, Infra 8, Product 12, Sales/CS 18, Finance/Ops 7 (total 97)
- Aggressive (hiring to meet demand): Eng IC 62, SRE 16, Infra 14, Product 18, Sales/CS 28, Finance/Ops 10 (total 148)

Month-level FTE burn waterfall (example month):
- Fixed payroll (base FTE comp): $2,980,000
- Benefits & payroll tax (~22%): $655,600
- GPU commit amortization & lease: $420,000 (commit tranche A)
- Cloud egress / storage / network: $125,000
- Hosting spot / burst compute: $330,000
- Sales credits & promotions (targeted): $60,000
- G&A / legal / misc: $95,000
- Total monthly operating burn (example): $4,665,600

Pricing sensitivity matrix (simplified - 3 SKU-weighted scenarios):
- Variables: token price (hosted microprice $/1k tokens), reserved commit mix (% of capacity committed), SKU elasticity factor (how demand shifts per price change)

Scenario A: Price compression (hosted price -25%)
- Hosted microprice baseline: $0.0020 per 1k tokens -> compressed to $0.0015
- Immediate effect: 8% increase in hosted demand (competitor price parity) but 16% gross margin erosion due to lower per-unit revenue and inability to fully offset with more efficient commits in short term
- Required FTE delta to support churn + ops (6 months): +9 Eng IC, +2 SRE (to handle higher request volume/batching)
- Runway impact: cash runway reduces by ~2.4 months vs baseline over 12 months without operational changes

Scenario B: Moderate price lift (+15%) with better commit mix
- Hosted microprice $0.0023 per 1k tokens
- Demand elasticity: -5% (some customers optimize down) but per-token margin improves by +9ppt; combined with moving 30% of capacity to 1-year commit, unit cost falls 10%
- Headcount delta: hiring deferred by 3 Eng IC in first 6 months
- Runway impact: runway extends by ~1.6 months, margin headroom allows buffer to accelerate some infra investments

Scenario C: Reserved-heavy optimization (commit bumps to 55% of capacity, price unchanged)
- Commits reduce marginal compute cost by 18% at high utilization; but fixed commit amortization increases fixed monthly burn by $520k
- Breakeven utilization threshold: 68% sustained utilization required to justify commits; below that commits worsen cash position
- Sensitivity band: +/- 6% utilization changes swing free cash by +/- $1.1M over 6 months

Attrition & hiring model (monthly steps):
- For each role: begin_month_FTEs - (FTEs * 1.0% attrition) + new_hires_adjusted_for_lag = end_month_FTEs
- Onboarding productivity ramp: new hires are at 40% productivity month 1, 65% month 2, 90% month 3, full at month 4 for engineering roles
- Attrition stress test: if attrition spikes to 18% annual (1.6% monthly), company needs +12 Eng IC hires over 6 months to keep baseline throughput; hiring capacity constrained by recruiting pipeline (max 8 hires/mo across Eng/Infra)

Scenario outputs (summary table text):
- Baseline: 12-month cash burn total (proj) = $56.7M; runway remaining = 14.4 months; avg gross margin = 46%
- Downside (Price -25%, attrition +50%): 12-month cash burn = $69.6M; runway = 9.1 months; avg gross margin = 38%
- Upside (Price +15% + commit optimization): 12-month cash burn = $50.2M; runway = 17.2 months; avg gross margin = 53%

Operational trigger rules (example):
- If 30-day realized utilization < 62% AND committed capacity > 40% -> initiate commit unwind conversation (60-day window)
- If hosted microprice falls > 15% vs baseline AND churn rate increases by > 3ppt in 30 days -> pause new hiring for non-critical infra roles; re-evaluate sales credit budget
- If realized attrition > 1.4% monthly for consecutive 2 months -> prioritize retention spend (targeted LTI / stay bonus) for critical subteams (serving runtime, SRE) and accelerate recruiting by +25% recruiter hours

Decision levers (to mitigate downside):
- Short term (0–3 months): tighten sales credits, shift non-customer critical compute to spot, temporary hiring freeze for product except critical roles, increase automated batching (software) to recover 6–8% unit cost
- Medium term (3–9 months): renegotiate commit tranches with cloud partner (smaller tranches, quarterly true-ups), cross-train infra to reduce headcount elasticity, launch price-tier experiment for mid-market customers with soft commitment offering
- Long term (9–18 months): invest in quantization/compilation features that reduce token cost by ~10–20% and create new reserved SKU pricing that bundles committed latency SLAs at a premium

Sensitivity notes and caveats:
- The model assumes SKU mix remains stable; large migrations of customer behavior (e.g., embeddings replacing chat) materially change the delta because per-token cost and throughput models differ
- GPU commit economics vary substantially by region and vendor; the $ figures above use a blended global view and should be regionalized per partner negotiation
- Hiring productivity assumptions are conservative for junior hires (ramp slower) and aggressive for senior hires (faster). Adjust by role when producing headcount hiring schedules.

Action items / next steps:
1) Finance-ops to regionalize the commit amortization model: produce region-by-region commit vs spot lane by 2026-12-10 (owner: Marina Lopez).
2) GTM to prepare two-tier pricing experiment (mid-market soft-commit + hosted-lite) and estimate conversion curves by 2026-12-17 (owner: Ravi Singh).
3) Eng ops to surface 6–8% immediate batching wins and a deployment plan to recover unit cost starting Jan 2027 (owner: Claire Dubois).
4) Consolidate monthly rolling workbook (this sheet) into FIN-1234 confluence with live links to hiring tracker and cloud-cost pipeline (owner: Ethan Walters).

Notes / scratch calculations (quick references):
- 1% monthly attrition on 48 Eng ICs ≈ 0.48 FTE lost per month -> ~5.8 FTE / year
- Onboarding 10 new Eng ICs (staggered) increases payroll run-rate by ~ $240k/mo (comp only) after full ramp
- Commit amortization examples: $6.24M 1-year commit amortized = $520k/mo extra fixed cost; marginal unit saving scenario at high utilization yields ~$0.00045 per 1k token in unit cost saved

Document history / provenance:
- Created as a cross-functional working sheet to support FY27 Q1 planning and price-experiment readiness; pulls from cloud cost pipeline (monthly exports), hiring tracker (recruiting sheet), and product SKU telemetry.
- Last updated with Q4 bookings cadence (2026-11-30) and revised attrition assumptions after HR pulse.
